title: One Tree — the input architecture
summary: Collapse the app's 16 hand-written per-surface pointer-dispatch functions into one tree walk; fixes the toast pointer bug and makes any layer (incl. plugin overlays) receive input.
description:
The app delivers pointer input through 16 hand-written per-surface dispatch functions (heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs: 8 chrome + 4 pane-header + 3 pane-viewport; plus dispatch_modal_pointer) and has NO input pass for ordinary layers at all — heca/src/chrome/layers_glue.rs runs rebuild/layout/paint and never input.

This phase collapses that into ONE retained tree with one dispatch/layout/paint/hint walk, using the capture→target→bubble traversal heca-grid-ui already provides (`dispatch()` in heca-grid-ui/src/component.rs). Overlays, modals and pane headers become nodes; adding a surface becomes adding a child. Done properly this DELETES the 16 functions rather than adding a 17th.

═══ WHY THIS IS FIRST, AND WHY IT IS NOT A NOTIFICATION PHASE ═══
Moved from F009 to F003 on 2026-08-28 — it was never notification-specific; notifications are only where it surfaced. It sits at the top of F003 because it is the foundation Antonio's FIRST RULE rests on: a component cannot own its own input until one dispatch walks the tree.

TWO SILENT FAILURES IN TWO DAYS, one new surface, two different subsystems:
1. The toast stack receives zero pointer events, so its × and action buttons never fire and hover falls through to the pane beneath (heca/src/chrome/notification_layer.rs mounts a Persistent, non-modal layer; nothing dispatches to it).
2. `prefix+/` lettered ONLY the toast — the hint walk read every visible layer's root box as an occluder, and a ToastStack is Pct(1.0) square because it POSITIONS its cards, not because it covers the screen. Fixed 2026-08-28 by reading the layer's own `covers_content` declaration, which the action router already honoured and the hint walk did not.

That is the shape of the defect: rebuild, layout, paint, hints and input are five separate walks over the layer stack, each with its own idea of what a layer means, and nothing checking they agree. Every new surface — a plugin's overlay included — must get it right in each one, and gets no error when it does not.

═══ THE AUTHORITY ═══
`docs/surface-compositor.md` § 0 — the whole picture, and what AGENTS.md already flags as required reading before adding any layer or surface. Read it before planning any task here. It carries the model, the four passes, the two repeatedly-proposed wrong designs and why, what the `Overlay` widget already provides, the record-and-perform seam for GPU content, today-vs-target, and the plugin plumbing-vs-capability split.

DONE 2026-08-28: `docs/input-architecture.md` was folded into it whole (now a redirect stub) so there is one voice rather than two, and AGENTS.md § 0d carries the FIRST RULE.

⚠️ CORRECTION: an earlier version of this description said `docs/hint-architecture.md` asserts "No second dispatch path" and that this is false. It is NOT false. Read in context, that sentence is about a **pick** propagating through the existing walk rather than introducing its own — which is correct. It is *pointer* input that has sixteen paths, not the picker. That doc needs no change.

═══ SCOPE, AND WHAT IS NOT HERE ═══
Priority order (sizes and risks on the individual tasks): T494+T495 (layer roots as tree children, modal as a swallowing node) fix the reported toast bug, touch neither the terminal nor the pane headers, and land first. Then T496 (chrome's 8 functions), T497 (pane header), T499 (HintSurface collapses to a tree path — 25 match sites across four files).

**T498 is CANCELED.** "Terminal viewport becomes a leaf node" duplicated P094(F011)/T449 from the input end. T449 is the fuller statement: `Terminal::new("name")` as a real component, placeable in a dock, an overlay or a plugin panel, owning its mouse, selection and prefix keys internally. **P097 owns the dispatch; P094 owns the terminal**, and P094 depends on this phase — its handoff carries the scene-seam decision and the ordering.

T501/T502 are the plugin-capability half: a described plugin overlay gets input for free once this lands, but it still cannot BUILD what the exposé builds — `CardGrid` has no declarative arm and 13 of 46 grid-ui widgets cannot be described at all. Until one of our own overlays is built the way a plugin must build it (T502), "plugins can add overlays" is a claim, not a fact.

⚠️ MUST NOT be interleaved with the oversized-file splits — T466/T468/T470/T471/T472 carve up the same files (component.rs's router, event.rs, app/interaction.rs) and are deferred until this lands.

VERIFICATION: input routing is exactly where green tests prove nothing — the toast received no events for an unknown time and nothing errored. Antonio drives every surface's mouse behaviour (T500).
notes:
**Handoff context update:**
T494 is functionally COMPLETE and driven on screen by Antonio: every surface (toast, exposé, command palette, OverlayHost modals + context menus) is a child of AppState::window_root, so the one capture→target→bubble walk delivers its pointer input. The reported toast bug (dead ×, hover falling through) is fixed. layout_layers, paint_layers, the separate layer scene and its second render_chrome flush, DynamicLayer::root/root_mut/opacity/is_leaving, visible_roots_mut, top_modal_root_mut and LayerContent are DELETED. The frost became a surface property (Overlay::frosted) before the move, which is what stopped it breaking. One regression was found by driving and fixed (a34ca0b): the registry was ticking surfaces the tree already ticked.

**Remaining work:**
T495 (modal as a node that swallows) is next and NOT started: dispatch_modal_pointer still exists in heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs and modal keyboard still routes through LayerRegistry::top_modal_node_mut in heca/src/app/events.rs rather than the tree walk. Then T496 (chrome's 8 dispatch functions), T497 (pane header), T499 (HintSurface collapses to a tree path), T500 (Antonio drives every surface).
decisions: A surface is PLACED, never registered: chrome::place_surface puts it in the window root, keyed, replacing in place under the same key; chrome::remove_surface takes it out.

The window root lives on AppState, is NOT an Option, and the chrome is its child 0 rather than the root itself — the chrome is rebuilt on resize/sidebar-toggle/theme-reload and dropped outright by reload_config, so a surface parented to it would lose its open state, its half-played arrival and its focus.
seat_chrome finds the chrome slot BY KEY, not by position: a surface may be placed before the first chrome exists (the toast mounts at startup) and a positional child 0 would seat the chrome over it.

InteractionSource::Surface carries a SurfaceKey derived from the key a surface declares, not a LayerId — a registry id stops existing once a surface is a node, and a plugin can declare a key but can never obtain a LayerId. Derived from what the caller holds rather than looked up, because a surface builds its emitter BEFORE registering.

The registry keeps ONLY name, nesting, modality, covers_content, visibility and the ViewNode a described surface was described by. The live tree is a child of the window root, found by chrome::surface_node(_mut).
THE TREE TICKS; THE REGISTRY ONLY RECONCILES — leaving_before_tick() before window_root.tick(dt), retire_finished_exits() after. The registry must never advance a surface again.
The frost is Overlay::frosted(true), recorded into the scene's BASE band (never the deferred overlay band) and performed by the host between the base flush and the overlay band.

tasks.title: Layer roots become children of the one tree
tasks.description:
GOAL: every registered surface is a node in the single retained tree, so the existing capture→target→bubble walk delivers pointer input to it.

═══ STATE 2026-08-31: SHIPPED, WITH ONE OPEN REGRESSION ═══

**The reported toast bug is FIXED and verified on screen by Antonio** — the × closes, action buttons fire, hover no longer falls through to the pane beneath.

Commits, in order:
- `f5f2262` — the frost became a surface property (`Overlay::frosted`) and the window root was introduced. `RetainedChrome` holds only what a chrome *build* produced; `AppState::window_root` is the one retained tree and is not an Option, because the chrome is rebuilt on resize/sidebar-toggle/theme-reload and dropped outright by `reload_config` — a surface parented to any of that would be destroyed with it.
- `0c45480` — the toast stack placed via `chrome::place_surface` instead of registered. `InteractionSource::Surface` carries a `SurfaceKey` (derived from the key a surface declares) instead of a `LayerId`, because a registry id stops existing once a surface is a node. `AppState::notification_layer_id` and `LayerId::for_test` deleted with their last callers.
- `971b1e2` — **the remaining three surfaces** (exposé, command palette, `OverlayHost` modals + context menus). Trees moved into the window root; `LayerRegistry` keeps name/nesting/modality/`covers_content`. Deleted: `layout_layers`, `paint_layers`, the separate layer scene and its second `render_chrome` flush, `DynamicLayer::root`/`root_mut`/`opacity`/`is_leaving`, `visible_roots_mut`, `top_modal_root_mut`, `LayerContent`.

Gate green throughout (667 heca tests; clippy at the two known pre-existing warnings).

═══ ⚠️ OPEN REGRESSION — Antonio, driving, 2026-08-31 ═══

Introduced by `971b1e2`. **The exposé's animation:**
1. Zoom-OUT stalls at roughly 10–15% opacity.
2. **Moving the mouse completes it** — so nothing is requesting the next frame, and any input event kicks it. That is a frame-scheduling symptom, not an animation-maths one.
3. After the first open, subsequent zoom-INs show the same stall.
4. After that, `ctrl+h/j/k/l` are broken too.

PRIME SUSPECT, unverified — instrument before changing code:
- **A hidden surface is still a child of the window root.** `layout_layers`/`paint_layers` used to filter on `visible`, so a hidden layer was inert. Now its node stays in the tree: it is still ticked, still walked, and can still hold `Base::focused` — which would explain (4), the keys going to a surface that is not on screen.
- **Double tick.** `heca/src/app/lifecycle.rs:111` `state.window_root.tick(dt)` now ticks every surface as a child, and `:127` `state.layers.tick(&mut state.window_root, dt)` ticks them again. Two advances per frame, and the registry's `was_leaving`/`still_leaving` transition is read around only one of them — so the frame an exit *finishes* can be missed, and with it the `fading = true` that requests the frame which paints its absence.

Both are consequences of the same thing: the registry's tick was written when it owned the trees and nothing else walked them.

VERIFY (Antonio drives; green tests prove nothing here): exposé open/close animation over several cycles, `ctrl+h/j/k/l` inside a dialog after an exposé cycle, the context menu, the confirm dialog, the command palette, and `prefix+/` landing on the front surface only.

═══ NOT IN THIS TASK ═══
`T495` (modal as a node that swallows) is still open: modal **keyboard** still routes through `LayerRegistry::top_modal_node_mut` rather than the tree walk, and `dispatch_modal_pointer` still exists.

statusLog.title: in-progress → planned (checkpoint saved)
statusLog.description:
Reason: T494 cannot land before the scene seam exists. The frost backdrop blurs whatever is behind an exposé, and needs a point in the frame where the scene holds everything beneath the surface and nothing of it. That point exists today only because chrome and layers paint into two separate scenes. Move layers into one tree and they paint in one continuous walk — the moment disappears and the frost breaks the instant T494 lands, unless a node can first say "blur what is behind me here" and let the host perform it. That is exactly this task's seam.
What was being done: Read only, no code. Established: (1) the task's stated approach — chrome root owns the layers, or a window root above both — fights the registry's design; (2) the registry is itself a parallel tree, storing parent links and re-deriving nesting every frame via z_path, duplicating what child position gives free; (3) blast radius is 21 LayerId references across 8 files and 18 layer-root accesses across 6; (4) the `Overlay` widget already provides everything the registry does — modal capture, fall-through, show/hide, animation, keyboard, occlusion geometry, and nesting — except reach outside the chrome tree; (5) the layout engine already supports absolutely-positioned children that take no space, so layers as stacked children need no new layout capability. All of it is written up in docs/surface-compositor.md § 0 and committed (9f40fb7), together with heca/tests/surface_drift.rs, which fails the build when a new surface is registered instead of placed.
Resume location: heca/src/chrome/layers_glue.rs (the three passes, no input pass); heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs:28 (dispatch_modal_pointer, the only layer input path); heca/src/app/events.rs (the hand-ordered pointer sequence); heca/src/app/render.rs:1045-1075 (the frost pass that forces the ordering).
How to resume: Do T448 first. Then rewrite this task against the real plan rather than its current text: overlays become ordinary children (the Overlay widget already handles modal capture, fall-through, nesting, animation and keyboard), the registry shrinks to a name-to-node lookup so show_layer/hide_layer keep working, and input becomes one walk from the root. Read docs/surface-compositor.md § 0 rather than re-deriving any of it.

tasks.title: Modal becomes a node that swallows what it does not handle
tasks.description:
GOAL: delete dispatch_modal_pointer (heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs:28) and the keyboard special-casing for top_modal in heca/src/app/events.rs. A modal is just a node in the one tree that returns Handled::Yes for every event it does not otherwise consume, so nothing leaks to the page behind it.

CURRENT STATE:
- dispatch_modal_pointer: returns true when top_modal(state).is_some(), dispatches the raw event to state.layers.top_modal_root_mut(), marks full redraw. Callers in events.rs (CursorMoved ~245, MouseInput ~296/302, MouseWheel ~407) bail when it returns true.
- events.rs KeyboardInput (lines ~111-204): a big block that, when top_modal is Some and the key is not a prefix/hint sequence, routes the key to the modal via state.widget_keymap.deliver_press/deliver_release and returns.
- The modal band is real (ModalSpec/ModalResult/ModalAction, OverlayHost::open_modal). "There is no Modal widget" — Overlay is the base layer, Dialog composes it.

WORK:
- Give the overlay/dialog node a "block" property (it likely already has one — Overlay blocking is a layer property). When set, the node consumes any Event it does not hand to a child: pointer events outside its panel become a scrim hit (fires on_dismiss), pointer events on the panel route normally, keys route to the panel's focus and are swallowed if unhandled.
- Once that is true, remove dispatch_modal_pointer and its call sites; the one-tree pointer walk from the sibling task already delivers into the modal node.
- Remove the KeyboardInput top_modal block; keys reach the focused modal node through normal focus-based delivery (the modal holds Base::focused while open, per the event model). Keep only the prefix/hint-pick fall-through (a modal must still be reachable by the universal hint picker).
- ModifiersChanged broadcast to the modal (events.rs ~226) is handled the same way — a Dialog tracks its own modifiers; if the tree walk delivers ModifiersChanged this becomes automatic.

PRESERVE: Esc / scrim-click dismiss, Tab/Shift+Tab focus cycling inside a Dialog, Ctrl+h/j/k/l inside a Dialog, the universal prefix+/ hint picker reaching a modal's buttons, and that a right-press that just opened the context menu is not also forwarded to the terminal.

VERIFY: Antonio drives — open the confirm dialog, click a button, Esc, scrim-click, Tab between buttons, prefix+/ onto a dialog button, and confirm the terminal never sees a stray click while a modal is up.

tasks.title: Chrome's 8 dispatch functions collapse into the walk
tasks.description:
GOAL: delete the 8 chrome_dispatch_* functions in heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs and route chrome pointer/widget input through the single tree walk.

CURRENT STATE (heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs):
- chrome_dispatch_press / button_press / button_release / release / move / wheel / cancelled / widget — each takes state.chrome_tree.as_mut() and calls heca_grid_ui::dispatch(&mut tree.root, &Event::...). They differ only in which Event they build and whether they return Handled.
- chrome_dispatch_widget sends Event::Widget(intent) to the chrome root (the focused FocusScope gates it into its subtree).
- Callers: heca/src/app/events.rs (CursorMoved/MouseInput/MouseWheel/CursorLeft) and heca/src/app/interaction.rs (the widget-intent path).

WORK:
- Once the window has one root (sibling task 1), chrome_tree is a subtree of it. A single dispatch(root, raw_event) reaches chrome the same as everything else.
- events.rs builds ONE Event::Raw per device event (raw_pointer / wheel_event already exist) and dispatches it into the root. Delete the per-kind chrome_dispatch_* calls.
- Event::Widget(intent) still goes to the root once; the focused FocusScope still decides where. Keep chrome_dispatch_widget's semantics (a false return is a legitimate "nothing scrollable, do not fall through to the pane") but express it as one dispatch into the root.
- Keep the pane-header-button / viewport-widget / divider-resize early-return checks in events.rs MouseInput for now — those are separate surfaces handled by their own tasks (pane header task, terminal viewport task). This task is chrome_tree only.

PRESERVE: sidebar hover affordances (MarkerGroup grip cue, Row hover) updating on move; a press consumed by the sidebar scrollbar thumb not also being read as a press on the card behind it; a release reaching the chrome tree wherever the cursor drifted (so a grabbed thumb releases); wheel over a hovered sidebar scroll region consuming and not also scrolling the terminal.

VERIFY: Antonio drives the sidebar — hover cues, click a row, scroll the sidebar, drag a column, drag the sidebar scrollbar thumb and release off it.

tasks.title: Pane header becomes a child of its pane
tasks.description:
GOAL: the per-pane info-bar header stops being a separate retained tree with its own dispatch functions and becomes a child node of its pane in the one tree. Delete dispatch_pane_header_move / press / release / wheel (heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs).

CURRENT STATE:
- state.pane_headers: HashMap<PaneId, PaneHeader> — each PaneHeader.root is its own retained tree, laid out and painted per pane, hit-tested by rect_contains(h.root.base().bounds, point).
- dispatch_pane_header_press returns Some((PaneId, consumed)) — consumed=true when an action button handled it, so events.rs does not forward that press to the terminal. dispatch_pane_header_move returns whether the pointer is over any header. Release + wheel are wired "in case" (nothing there grabs the pointer or scrolls today).
- heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs builds the trees; heca/src/chrome/pane/ is the pane-as-retained-component work (mod/model/shell/testing).
- events.rs MouseInput has an early-return: a plain left-press that hits a header action button is consumed; a press on the empty header band falls through and focuses the pane (chrome, no terminal selection).

WORK:
- Make the header a child of the pane component (heca/src/chrome/pane/). The pane node already exists in the tree; the header hangs off it.
- The one-tree walk then delivers press/move/release/wheel to the header for free. Delete the four dispatch_pane_header_* functions and the pane_headers HashMap iteration.
- The "press on the band focuses the pane, press on a button runs the action, neither reaches the terminal as selection" behaviour becomes: the band node handles the press (emits focus), the button handles its own click, and the pane leaf below only sees what bubbles past — which is nothing, because the header consumed it.

RISK — PERFORMANCE, NOT CORRECTNESS: the per-pane retained header trees exist for damage tracking and paint caching. Folding them into the one tree can regress frame time, and the exposé is already reported laggy with many panes (F003/P082/T421). Measure frame time with 8+ panes before and after. If it regresses, the header still becomes a child but keeps its own damage/cache boundary within the tree.

PRESERVE: action button hover affordance on move; a button press not leaking to the terminal; the lower pane's header band sitting on the divider not breaking divider/resize gestures (the resize check in events.rs runs after the header-button check — keep that order or fold the divider in too).

VERIFY: Antonio drives — click each header action button, hover them, press the empty band (focuses, no selection), and resize a divider whose top edge is under a header band.

tasks.title: Terminal viewport becomes a leaf node
tasks.description:
THE DANGEROUS ONE. The terminal viewport is the product. Its mouse path carries PTY mouse reporting, host-grid selection, scrollback, and click-to-focus, and it has the LEAST test coverage of anything here because it is all interactive. A dropped event makes the terminal feel broken with no failing test. Sequence this LAST of the plumbing tasks and give Antonio a long driving pass.

GOAL: the terminal viewport is an ordinary leaf node in the one tree for layout, hit-testing and event delivery. Its PAINT stays special — it still renders through the GPU terminal path (heca-renderer, cosmic-text atlas), not a Scene DrawCommand list. Delete dispatch_pane_viewport_move / press / release (heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs).

CURRENT STATE:
- Panes are GPU terminal surfaces, not grid-ui widgets. events.rs MouseInput/CursorMoved/MouseWheel route to the terminal via forward_mouse_button / forward_mouse_move / forward_mouse_wheel (heca/src/app/terminal_host.rs) AFTER a chain of early-return checks (modal, pane-header button, viewport widget, divider resize).
- dispatch_pane_viewport_* handle the retained widgets that overlay the terminal (scrollbar, badge) — a plain left-press on one intercepts before divider-resize / content forwarding; returns whether it was consumed so the terminal is left alone.
- heca/src/mouse/ owns hit_test_pane, on_cursor_moved, on_mouse_input, resize gestures, interactive-move, edge scroll.
- mouse reporting: when the TUI has requested mouse events, forward_mouse_* translates and sends them to the PTY. Selection: host-grid selection starts/extends on drag when the TUI is not grabbing the mouse. Scrollback: wheel scrolls the host viewport unless terminal_mouse forwards it. Click-to-focus: a press on a pane focuses it.

WORK:
- The pane node (heca/src/chrome/pane/) gets a terminal-viewport leaf child with real bounds. The one-tree walk hit-tests it and delivers Click/Scroll/Drag/PointerEnter to it.
- The leaf's handlers call into the existing heca/src/mouse/ + terminal_host.rs logic — this task RE-HOMES the entry point, it does not rewrite mouse reporting or selection.
- The scrollbar/badge widgets that overlay the terminal become children of the same pane node above the terminal leaf, so normal bubbling gives them the press first and the terminal leaf only sees what they did not take. Delete dispatch_pane_viewport_*.
- Divider resize: fold the divider hit into the tree too (a thin node between panes) or keep it as the one remaining host check — decide during implementation, but do not leave it as a fourth parallel dispatch.

PRESERVE, EACH DRIVEN BY ANTONIO SEPARATELY: PTY mouse reporting (a TUI that wants clicks gets them, with correct cell coords), host-grid selection (click-drag selects, double/triple-click, shift-click extend), scrollback wheel, click-to-focus, Ctrl/Cmd+wheel font zoom intercept, edge auto-scroll during a pane drag, interactive-move modifier drag, and vim working (Escape reaching the program).

VERIFY: a full interactive pass. Green tests prove nothing here.

Duplicates P094(F011)/T449 from the other side. This task framed the terminal as "a leaf node the one dispatch can reach"; T449 makes the Terminal a real component — `Terminal::new("name")`, placeable in a dock, an overlay or a plugin panel, owning its own mouse, selection and prefix keys internally. That is the same work described from the input end, and T449 is the fuller statement of it.

Antonio, 2026-08-28, as the project's FIRST RULE: a DOM-like structure you can place anywhere, where no other developer handles clicks, surfaces or mouse-move — it MUST be internal logic, abstracted. That applies to every widget and component, present and future, not to the terminal alone.

So the dependency runs one way: P094/T449 needs this phase's tree dispatch to exist before a component can receive input without the host routing to it. P097 owns the dispatch; P094 owns the terminal. Nothing here is lost — the terminal's PTY forwarding, selection and mouse reporting move verbatim into its own handlers as part of T449.

tasks.title: HintSurface collapses to a tree path
tasks.description:
GOAL: the prefix+/ hint system stops enumerating surfaces and walks the one tree. Delete the HintSurface enum arms and the ~25 match sites that each list the roots.

CURRENT STATE (heca/src/chrome/hint/):
- hint/surfaces.rs — ~12 match sites over a HintSurface enum (one arm per surface: chrome, panes, each layer kind, pane header, ...).
- hint/targets.rs — ~7 match sites collecting hint targets per surface.
- hint/visibility.rs — ~4 match sites deciding which surface's hints are shown (e.g. "not the sidebar while a pane is zoomed or a toast is up").
- hint/letters.rs — ~2 match sites assigning letters.
- Total ~25 sites. Adding a surface means adding an arm to each; a miss is a silently un-hintable surface.
- The layer stack already models occlusion as tree position ("z is a path, not a band"); hint visibility should read the same tree, not a parallel enum.
- NOTE (heca-57, 2026-08-27): the sidebar hint-letter instability is ALREADY FIXED on the grid-ui side and is NOT part of this task. Cause was naming: a container declared with scope_key (what a dock does) contributed nothing to its children's names because the naming fn read only key, so two docks holding the same workspace produced identical name sets and a remembered letter bounced between copies. Fixed centrally in heca-grid-ui — a widget now has one declared name (key, else scope_key) and every namer reads it (also closed T482). Do not re-investigate letter stability here.

WORK:
- Once input is one tree walk (tasks 1-5), hint collection is one walk too: descend the tree, collect every hintable node (Base already carries hintable + the pick intent since the cards went into the tree), in paint order, honouring occlusion by tree position.
- Replace HintSurface with a tree path / node handle. hint/surfaces.rs, targets.rs, letters.rs collapse to a single traversal.
- hint/visibility.rs rules ("hide the sidebar's hints while a covering layer is up") become "a node occluded by a covering sibling is not collected" — read from the tree, not special-cased per surface.
- KeyHintGroup / the notification.pick precise picker (heca/src/chrome/notification_layer.rs wraps the stack in a KeyHintGroup bound to notification_pick_open) still works — it is a sub-scope within the same walk.

PRESERVE: prefix+/ letters on every clickable chrome button, on toast action buttons and the x, on pane-picker targets; the KeyHint being a UNIVERSAL overlay for any clickable widget (never column/ws/pane-specific); a covering overlay hiding the hints of what it covers.

Our flagship overlay does not use the plugin path at all, so it proves the layer stack and proves NOTHING about whether a plugin could build one. This is the Rule Zero check: until one of our overlays is built the way a plugin must, the capability is unverified.

DEPENDS ON: the one-tree input work (T494-T499) so a described node actually receives input, and the declarative-widget-arms task (T501) so the overlay's widgets can be described.

## What was being done

The app delivered pointer input through **16 hand-written per-surface dispatch functions**
(`heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs`: 8 chrome + 4 pane-header + 3 pane-viewport, plus
`dispatch_modal_pointer`) and had **no input pass for ordinary layers at all**. This phase collapses
that into **one retained tree** with one dispatch / layout / paint / hint walk. Done properly it
**DELETES** the 16 rather than adding a 17th. It is F003's priority 0 because it is the foundation
the FIRST RULE rests on (AGENTS.md § 0d): *a component cannot own its own input until one dispatch
walks the tree.*

### What is now BUILT — **`docs/surface-compositor.md` § 0 is the record, not this handoff**

§ 0 was rewritten on 2026-08-31 to describe the built state. **Read it; it is not duplicated here.**

- **§ 0.1 / § 0.6** — every surface is a node in `AppState::window_root`; `chrome::place_surface` /

  key rather than position; what the registry still holds.
- **§ 0.7** — ⚠️ **THE TREE TICKS; THE REGISTRY ONLY RECONCILES**, and the regression that rule comes
  from. **Read this before touching the frame loop.**
- **§ 0.5** — the record-and-perform seam. The frost is now `Overlay::frosted(true)`, recorded in the
  scene's BASE band and performed by the host between the base flush and the overlay bands; that is
  what stopped it breaking when the two scenes became one.
- **§ 9** — the registry section, now marked as history.

Two things that are decisions rather than architecture, so they live here:

- **`InteractionSource::Surface` carries a `SurfaceKey`** (a `u64` derived from the key a surface
  declares) instead of a `LayerId`, so `InteractionSource` stays `Copy` across its ~172 call sites. A
  registry id stops existing once a surface is a node; a plugin can declare a key and can never
  obtain a `LayerId` (⭐⭐ RULE ZERO — `HintTargetId` was deleted for exactly this shape). **Derived,
  never looked up:** a surface builds its emitter *before* it registers, so a lookup would answer
  `surface:7` then and `heca.expose` after — one surface with two identities, and the policy's
  `source != Surface(active_context)` comparison would silently stop matching.
- **Deleted with the move:** `layout_layers`, `paint_layers`, the separate layer scene **and its
  second `render_chrome` flush**, `DynamicLayer::root`/`root_mut`/`opacity`/`is_leaving`,
  `visible_roots_mut`, `top_modal_root_mut`, `LayerContent`,
  `LayerBackdrop`/`set_backdrop`/`wants_frost`/`frost_opacity`, `AppState::notification_layer_id`,

- **Hover holds the stack still.** `ToastStack::hovered_signal(Signal<bool>)` reports whether the
  pointer is on a card; `NotificationRuntime::set_hovered` decides what it costs. A **pause, not a
